sentences: B2B quick commerce startup Zorit, formerly known as Bijnis, has raised nearly Rs 27 crore ($2.84 million) in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital.
The investment also saw participation from existing backers Info Edge and WaterBridge, along with Better Capital, angel investors, and company employees.

The funding round attracted several prominent angel investors, including Anupam Mittal, founder of Shaadi.com, the founders of Shiprocket, Mohit Sardana, CEO of Xpressbees, and Sarthak Misra of SoftBank.
Following the latest investment, Info Edge's stake in Bijnis is set to increase to 20.12 percent on a fully converted and diluted basis.
In a stock exchange disclosure earlier this week, Info Edge also indicated the possibility of acquiring additional equity in the company through a secondary transaction.

Founded in 2015 by Siddharth Vij, Chaitanya Rathi, Siddharth Rastogi and Sachin Chauhan, the company initially operated as a business-to-business marketplace connecting manufacturers with offline retailers .
However, it shifted to an inventory-led quick commerce model in late 2024, focusing on faster product sourcing and inventory replenishment for retailers.
Under its current business model, Zorit allows offline retailers to procure products from nearby dark stores, with deliveries completed in as little as 60 minutes.
The company currently operates 12 dark stores across 12 cities and has achieved annualised sales of Rs 120 crore.
According to the company, nearly half of its dark stores have reached break-even, including the costs associated with liquidating unsold inventory.
Zorit also reported changes in retailer adoption and purchasing behaviour following its business model transition.
Nearly 60 percent of its retail partners had not previously used an online B2B platform.
Retailer retention beyond the sixth month has improved fourfold compared with the earlier marketplace model, while monthly ordering frequency has increased fivefold.

The fresh capital will be directed towards strengthening the company's quick commerce infrastructure, broadening its product assortment and increasing engagement with offline retailers across its existing markets.
Siddharth Vij, CEO, Zorit said , “We strongly believe that a substantial part of India’s future commerce will remain retailer led.

As consumer expectations evolve, retailers need better technology and supply chain infrastructure to compete and grow,”
The company's funding history includes investments from Matrix Partners, now known as Z47, Sequoia Capital, now Peak XV Partners, and WestBridge Capital.
In September 2021, Bijnis raised $30 million in a Series B funding round led by WestBridge Capital, taking its total funding to more than $40 million.
However, Info Edge had written off its entire Rs 76.65 crore investment in Bijnis, operated by Bizcrum Infotech Pvt Ltd, in May 2023.

Bengaluru-based tea and beverage chain Boba Bhai recorded a 139 percent increase in revenue from operations to Rs 68 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, compared with Rs 28.44 crore in FY25.
However, the company's losses also widened during the period as it continued to invest in business expansion and strengthen its retail footprint.
Food and beverage sales remained the primary contributor to its operating revenue, increasing 137.1 percent to Rs 67.26 crore in FY26.
The category accounted for approximately 99 percent of the company's total operating revenue.
Revenue from scrap sales also increased to Rs 28 lakh during the fiscal year, compared with Rs 7 lakh in FY25.
Additionally, Boba Bhai reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 69 crore from Rs 29.44 crore in the previous financial year.
On the expenditure front, the company's costs increased across major categories as it expanded its operations.
Cost of materials consumed, its largest expense component, rose 138.5 percent to Rs 25 crore in FY26.
Employee benefit expenses recorded a sharper increase of 210.3 percent to Rs 13.5 crore, reflecting higher workforce-related costs.
Advertising and promotional expenses climbed 139.9 percent to Rs 13 crore, while commission expenses increased 155.9 percent to Rs 11.44 crore during the year.
Other expenses, which contributed around 35 percent of the company's total expenditure, rose 120.3 percent to Rs 31.46 crore.
Overall, Boba Bhai's total expenses increased more than twofold to Rs 90.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 39 crore in FY25.
The company had 188 employees as of March 2026.
Despite the growth in revenue, the increase in operating costs affected its bottom line.
Boba Bhai's net losses widened 2.2 times to Rs 21.8 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 9.96 crore in the previous fiscal year.
The company, however, reported a marginal improvement in operating efficiency.
Its expenditure to generate every rupee of operating revenue declined to Rs 1.33 in FY26 from Rs 1.37 in FY25.
Its EBITDA margin also improved to -30.35 percent from -34.67 percent during the corresponding period.
However, return on capital employed (ROCE) deteriorated to -41.12 percent from -32.47 percent.
The company's cash and bank balances also witnessed a significant decline, falling to Rs 2.85 crore in FY26 from Rs 24.07 crore in the previous fiscal year.
The financial performance comes as Boba Bhai continues to expand its store network across India.
The company raised Rs 40 crore in March 2026 to support its expansion plans and strengthen its business operations.
Currently, Boba Bhai operates approximately 100 stores across eight cities.
The company plans to increase its presence to 10 cities in FY27 and add another 150-200 stores by the end of the financial year.

Tilaknagar Industries Limited (TI) reported net revenue of Rs 2,059 crore in the first half of FY27, marking a 180 percent year-on-year (YoY) increase, as the company continued to integrate Imperial Blue Whisky into its operations.
The company's second-quarter performance also saw Imperial Blue gain over 100 basis points in all-India market share.
For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, TI recorded net revenue of Rs 1,033 crore, up 172 percent YoY, after adjusting for subsidy.
Sales volume reached 8.9 million cases, representing 160 percent growth compared with the same period last year.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) stood at Rs 146 crore, up 143 percent YoY, with a margin of 14.1 percent.
Profit after tax, excluding exceptional items and amortization related to the Imperial Blue acquisition, increased 26 percent to Rs 66 crore.
The company said that the states that transitioned from the Transition Services and Manufacturing Agreement (TSMA) following the first quarter had stabilised under its operations.
The final remaining state is expected to transition by the end of FY27, which could further support the integration process.
While primary volumes remained largely flat during the quarter, secondary volumes grew 7.8 percent sequentially.
Imperial Blue Whisky recorded 8.5 percent quarter-on-quarter growth, while Mansion House Brandy reported a 7.1 percent increase.
Imperial Blue gained market share across 17 states, with Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Assam and Rajasthan among the key contributors.
Mansion House Brandy also became the leading brandy across price points in Karnataka in September 2026, according to the company.
Amit Dahanukar, Chairman and Managing Director of Tilaknagar Industries , said the operational transition had progressed and the company's brands continued to expand their reach.
"With the states transitioned out of TSMA after Q1 now stabilised, we have taken another decisive step towards completing the Imperial Blue integration.

Our secondary volumes grew by 7.8 percent during the quarter, and Imperial Blue continued to gain market share across the country, reflecting the strength of our brands and the reach of our expanded distribution network," Dahanukar said.
However, the company continued to face cost pressures from packaging materials, particularly glass.
Prices of extra neutral alcohol (ENA), a key input for spirits production, also began rising towards the end of the quarter due to higher fuel and grain costs.
TI said its EBITDA margin would have been approx 16.5 percent without the impact of inflationary pressures.
